## Scope and relation to the paper

This is a parallel experiment using the zero-shift construction in
`kappa0func.Rmd`. It leaves the original four positive-shift notebooks
unchanged. The equation is
$$
 u_t+\nu(-\Delta_\Gamma)^{\alpha/2}u=f,\qquad\kappa=0,
$$
on the connected tadpole with stem length 1 and loop length 2, with
continuity and Kirchhoff conditions. The fixed geometric gap scale is
$\gamma_*=2/(3\cdot2)=1/3$. It is independent of $h$ and $\tau$ and
introduces no reaction or decay of the constant mode.

The paper's rational construction applies at zero shift. Its reported
zero-shift numerical table, however, uses the **exact discrete spectral
power**, not BRASIL, and different single-mode data. The earlier agreement
with that table and the one-step sparse/modal check validate components
of this implementation; they are not convergence results for these new
studies. The tables generated here are additional zero-shift BRASIL
experiments. They must not be quoted as the paper's published slopes.

## Loading and running independently

Use `/usr/bin/Rscript` or the RStudio session containing `rSPDE`, `Matrix`,
`Rcpp`, `RcppEigen`, `knitr`, `rmarkdown`, and `ggplot2`. The system R used
for verification is distinct from the older `/usr/local/bin/Rscript`.
The setup extracts definitions from `kappa0func.Rmd` to a temporary file
and loads a private environment. It does not source `brasilfunc.R`, create
a persistent generated R library, or execute the helper notebook's demos.

```{r true-diff-cov-in-h-rough-as-in-mat-setup}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message=FALSE, warning=TRUE, error=FALSE, cache=FALSE,
                      dev="png", fig.width=8, fig.height=5)
for (package in c("Matrix","rSPDE","Rcpp","RcppEigen","ggplot2"))
    if (!requireNamespace(package,quietly=TRUE)) stop("Missing package: ",package)
true_diff <- local({
    extracted <- tempfile("true_diff_functions_",fileext=".R")
    on.exit(unlink(extracted),add=TRUE)
    knitr::purl("kappa0func.Rmd",output=extracted,quiet=TRUE,documentation=0L)
    functions <- new.env(parent=globalenv())
    sys.source(extracted,envir=functions)
    functions
})
```

Two explicitly labeled profiles are available. **Validation** is the
runnable default: it uses three exponents, smaller grids, and independent
implementation checks. **Paper** uses all nine exponents and the original
study's main mesh/time targets. Both use the same equations, solver, and
error definition. For smooth h/tau studies, the fixed rational order is
12 instead of the original positive-shift order 8, to reduce contamination
under the smaller gap scale. The full settings are printed below and
stored with results. A fitted slope alone does not certify that every
other error contribution is negligible.

To run this notebook at paper resolution, set the options before rendering:

```r
options(NAP.true_diff.profile="paper", NAP.true_diff.recompute=TRUE)
# rmarkdown::render("true_diff_cov_in_h_rough_as_in_mat.Rmd")
```

The paper-resolution rough study takes 1,250,000 solver steps **per case**.
Use the validation profile first. `workers` defaults to 1; edit the
parameter chunk or supply an explicit override to use independent forked
cases on Unix. Neither profile silently substitutes a closed modal
recurrence for the sparse rational evolution.

## Parameters

```{r true-diff-cov-in-h-rough-as-in-mat-parameters}
profile <- getOption("NAP.true_diff.profile","validation")
settings <- true_diff$kappa0_study_settings("rough_h",profile)
# Optional named overrides; the saved settings and cache identity include them.
overrides <- getOption("NAP.true_diff.overrides",list())
if (length(setdiff(names(overrides),names(settings)))) stop("Unknown setting override.")
for (name in names(overrides)) settings[[name]] <- overrides[[name]]
# For example: settings$workers <- 3L
settings_table <- data.frame(parameter=names(settings),
    value=vapply(settings,function(x) paste(x,collapse=", "),character(1)))
knitr::kable(settings_table)
```

## Rough forcing and its zero-shift analytical solution

Keep exactly the original rough data:
$$
 u_0=0,\qquad f=g=\sum_{j\ge1}j^{-1}\phi_j,\qquad
 \phi_j=0\text{ on the stem},\quad
 \phi_j(x)=\sin(2^j\pi x)\text{ on the loop }[0,2].
$$
These are orthonormal Kirchhoff eigenfunctions with eigenvalues
$\mu_j=\pi^2 2^{2j}$. Thus $g\in L_2$ but has no positive spectral
Sobolev regularity. Each mode has zero spatial mean, so the full solution
has zero mass for all time. With $a_j=\nu(\pi2^j)^\alpha$,
$$
 u_K(s,t)=\sum_{j=1}^K b_j(t)\phi_j(s),\qquad
 b_j(t)=\frac{1-e^{-a_jt}}{j a_j}.
$$
A fixed cutoff is used for every solver mesh, and is not added to the
measured error as a separate positive term.

On $h=2^{-J}$ aligned meshes, the sine-hat loads for $j\ge J$ vanish
analytically, including the two endpoint half-hats at the junction.
The infinite forcing therefore has the exact finite FEM load
$\sum_{j=1}^{J-1}j^{-1}(\phi_j,\psi_i)$.
The implementation evaluates these retained integrals analytically;
it does not obtain the rough load by sampling an underresolved series.

## Quarter-loop restriction and mean handling

As in the original rough notebook, solve only on $[0,1/2]$ with zero
endpoint values and extend by odd reflection and period one around the
loop; the stem remains zero. For example, the value on $(1/2,1)$ is
minus the reflected value on $(0,1/2)$. The full loop has four copies,
so the reduced matrices are four times the interval matrices. Their
mass norm equals the full-graph norm. This is an invariant FEM subspace,
not a truncation to discrete eigenfunctions.

No constant vector belongs to this restricted space. The shifted sparse
matrices are $G_{\rm red}/\gamma_*-z_nC_{\rm red}$, with the same
$\gamma_*=1/3$ and source-table logic as the full-space solver.
`kappa0_rough_operator()` constructs them; the compiled kernel uses
`split_mean=FALSE`. Subtracting a quarter-interval mean would change the
problem. Zero **full-graph** mean follows exactly from the antisymmetric
extension. The implementation check compares a reduced run with the
full connected tadpole and its integrated mass.

## Reference truncation and expected fractional rate

Require $K\ge\max J$ so every mesh's first unresolved mode remains in
the reference, and `reference_J >= K+2` to resolve the retained sines.
The reference is sampled on the same reduced physical interval, with
the same factor-four mass matrix and right-endpoint time sum as in the
original study. The same compressed sampled-error identity is used.
All backward Euler steps are advanced, including those between reference
times. See Section 10 of `kappa0func.Rmd` for the shared implementation.

The omitted reference tail satisfies
$$
 \|u-u_K\|_{L_2(0,T;L_2)}^2\le B_K=
 \frac{T}{\nu^2\pi^{2\alpha}}
 \frac{2^{-2\alpha(K+1)}}{(K+1)^2(1-2^{-2\alpha})}.
$$
The code requires $B_K/E^2\le0.002$ at **every** measured error.
This checks truncation only; it does not certify reference mesh or time
quadrature. The unresolved-mode tail and the resolved-mode FEM error
suggest $E_h\asymp h^\alpha/J$ for fixed $0<\alpha<2$, provided temporal
and rational errors are sufficiently small. Show raw errors and raw
slopes, then fit $\log(JE_h)=s_h\log h+b$ against the reference slope
$\alpha$. Multiplying by $J$ removes the predicted logarithmic factor;
it does not subtract an error contribution or modify the computed PDE.

The paper profile retains $J=5:9$, $K=16$, `reference_J=18`,
$\tau=8\cdot10^{-7}$, $\tau_\star=10^{-5}$, $m=14$, $\nu=1$.
The validation profile uses $J=5:8$, $K=12$, `reference_J=14`,
$\tau=2\cdot10^{-6}$ and $\tau_\star=2\cdot10^{-4}$, with the
same order 14 and diffusion 1. These settings are not interchangeable
when assessing small errors; saved profile identities prevent mixing them.

## Compute or load matching results

This chunk runs when knitting. Existing matching results are reused;
missing or stale results are recomputed. Filenames include the notebook
name and profile. The result identity includes the full settings, source
hashes, and numerical package versions, so other profiles and the
positive-shift studies cannot be loaded accidentally.

Before computation the checks compare compiled and R solutions for
fractional and integer powers, compare compressed and direct reference
quadratic forms, and compare the rough reduction with full-graph FEM.
Those are implementation checks; the displayed convergence results and
mass diagnostics provide separate evidence about the actual experiment.

```{r true-diff-cov-in-h-rough-as-in-mat-recompute-or-load}
result <- true_diff$kappa0_execute_study(settings,"true_diff_cov_in_h_rough_as_in_mat.Rmd",
    recompute=isTRUE(getOption("NAP.true_diff.recompute",FALSE)))
knitr::kable(result$validation,digits=12,caption="Independent implementation checks")
cat("Profile:",settings$profile,"\nGenerated:",result$generated_at,
    "\nComputation seconds:",round(result$elapsed_seconds,2),"\n")
```

## Results and fitted rates

The benchmark slopes describe the theoretical rate scale. The observed
fits use the computed data below; they are not replaced by the benchmark.
For smooth data, `max_mass_error` is the maximum absolute discrepancy from
the discrete mass recurrence over the entire trajectory. For the rough
reduction the full-graph mass is zero by symmetry, validated independently.

```{r true-diff-cov-in-h-rough-as-in-mat-rates}
knitr::kable(result$rates,digits=6)
```

```{r true-diff-cov-in-h-rough-as-in-mat-plot-results}
d <- result$results
d$alpha_label <- factor(d$alpha,levels=settings$alpha)
if (settings$study=="m") {
    p <- ggplot2::ggplot(d,ggplot2::aes(sqrt(m),error,colour=alpha_label,group=alpha_label))+
        ggplot2::geom_line()+ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(shape=resolved))+
        ggplot2::scale_y_log10()+ggplot2::labs(x="sqrt(m)",y="Isolated space-time L2 error",
            colour="alpha",shape="Resolved",title="Zero-shift rational convergence")
} else {
    p <- ggplot2::ggplot(d,ggplot2::aes(axis,error,colour=alpha_label,group=alpha_label))+
        ggplot2::geom_line()+ggplot2::geom_point()+ggplot2::scale_x_log10()+
        ggplot2::scale_y_log10()+ggplot2::labs(x=if(settings$study=="tau") "tau" else "h",
            y="Sampled space-time L2 error",colour="alpha",title="Zero-shift convergence")
}
# Reference curves retain their prescribed slope and are geometrically
# anchored to the data. They are guides, not additional computed errors.
guides <- do.call(rbind,lapply(settings$alpha,function(a) {
    x <- d[d$alpha==a,]
    power <- if(settings$study=="m") -2*pi*sqrt(a/2) else if(settings$study=="tau") 1 else 2
    xx <- if(settings$study=="m") sqrt(x$m) else log(x$axis)
    if(settings$study=="rough_h") power <- a
    x$guide <- exp(mean(log(x$error)-power*xx)+power*xx)
    x
}))
guides$alpha_label <- factor(guides$alpha,levels=settings$alpha)
p <- p+ggplot2::geom_line(data=guides,ggplot2::aes(y=guide),linetype="dashed",alpha=0.6)+
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size=12)+ggplot2::labs(subtitle=paste("kappa=0; gamma*=1/3;",settings$profile,"profile"))
print(p)
figure_dir <- file.path("data_files",paste0("true_diff_cov_in_h_rough_as_in_mat_",settings$profile))
dir.create(figure_dir,recursive=TRUE,showWarnings=FALSE)
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(figure_dir,"convergence.pdf"),p,width=8,height=5)
```

### Logarithmically corrected spatial errors

The raw-error plot above includes h-to-the-alpha guides for context;
the theoretical logarithmic correction is assessed in this second plot.
The corrected slopes are the `observed` column of the rate table.

```{r true-diff-cov-in-h-rough-as-in-mat-corrected-figure}
corrected_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(d,ggplot2::aes(axis,corrected_error,colour=alpha_label))+
    ggplot2::geom_line()+ggplot2::geom_point()+ggplot2::scale_x_log10()+ggplot2::scale_y_log10()+
    ggplot2::labs(x="h",y="J times sampled space-time L2 error",colour="alpha")+
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size=12)
corrected_guides <- do.call(rbind,lapply(settings$alpha,function(a) {
    x <- d[d$alpha==a,]; x$guide <- exp(mean(log(x$corrected_error)-a*log(x$axis)))*x$axis^a; x
}))
corrected_plot <- corrected_plot+ggplot2::geom_line(data=corrected_guides,
    ggplot2::aes(y=guide),linetype="dashed",alpha=0.6)
print(corrected_plot)
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(figure_dir,"corrected_convergence.pdf"),corrected_plot,width=8,height=5)
cat("Largest squared-tail fraction:",max(d$tail_squared_fraction),"\n")
```

## Sensitivity of the finest tested case

The validation profile refines the fixed solver and reference settings
one at a time at the finest tested primary axis value, for every exponent.
The table measures the change in the sampled error. It is a sensitivity
check, not a certified bound on an individual error contribution. The
isolated-m study instead has the independent modal and integer-power
controls above. Paper-resolution sensitivity runs are opt-in through
`settings$refinement_checks <- TRUE` because they can be expensive.

```{r true-diff-cov-in-h-rough-as-in-mat-sensitivity}
if (!is.null(result$refinement_checks)) {
    knitr::kable(result$refinement_checks,digits=9)
} else {
    cat("No additional discretization sensitivity run for these settings.\n")
}
```

knitr::kable(data.frame(package=names(result$package_versions),
                        version=unname(result$package_versions)))

The `.rds` file contains settings, errors, rates, validation values,
source hashes, versions, and the generation timestamp. PDF figures are
written to a matching profile-specific directory. To force a fresh run,
set `options(NAP.true_diff.recompute=TRUE)` before rendering. To check
other error budgets, override only the corresponding settings and save
that run under a separate output identity or copy its result before
changing parameters; never compare relabeled caches from different runs.
